ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Medication reconciliation before treatment

A patient beginning enoxaparin for postoperative thromboprophylaxis reports taking ibuprofen regularly for arthritis and aspirin without a current prescription. Which issue is most important to review before continuing this combination?

  1. Additive impairment of hemostasis and bleeding risk
  2. Neutralization of enoxaparin by acidic drugs
  3. Complete loss of antithrombin binding
  4. Mandatory development of immune HIT
  5. Prevention of all gastrointestinal bleeding
Answer and explanation

Additive impairment of hemostasis and bleeding risk

NSAIDs and antiplatelet agents can add bleeding risk during anticoagulation.

Option explanations

Additive impairment of hemostasis and bleeding risk: NSAIDs and antiplatelet agents can add bleeding risk during anticoagulation.

Neutralization of enoxaparin by acidic drugs: Acidic oral medicines do not simply neutralize injected enoxaparin.

Complete loss of antithrombin binding: The interaction is not complete loss of antithrombin binding.

Mandatory development of immune HIT: HIT is an immune syndrome, not an inevitable consequence of this combination.

Prevention of all gastrointestinal bleeding: These agents can increase rather than prevent gastrointestinal bleeding.
